artworks.title: Great Eleusinian Relief (Demeter, Triptolemus, and Persephone)
artworks.description: The monumental Pentelic-marble votive from Eleusis, now National Archaeological Museum, Athens (NAMA 126): Demeter offers ears of wheat to the youth Triptolemus while Persephone crowns him — the canonical image of the Eleusinian envoy who carries Demeter's gift of agriculture to humankind.

artworks.title: Triptolemus with Demeter and Persephone (Niobid Painter stamnos)
artworks.description: Attic red-figure stamnos by the Niobid Painter: Triptolemus stands between the two Eleusinian goddesses, the mortal youth framed by Demeter and Persephone as he prepares to carry the Mysteries' grain across the world.

artworks.title: Triptolemus in the Winged Chariot (name-vase of the Triptolemos Painter)
artworks.description: Louvre G 187, the eponymous cup of the Triptolemos Painter: the Eleusinian hero sits in his winged, serpent-drawn chariot — the image that fixed Triptolemus' mission in the Athenian imagination for a century of vase-painting.

artworks.title: Ceres Giving Her Chariot to Triptolemus
artworks.description: Tempesta's Ovidian etching (LACMA): Ceres entrusts her dragon-chariot to Triptolemus so he may sow grain among the nations — the Renaissance restaging of the Eleusinian mission from Metamorphoses Book V.

artworks.title: Lyncus Turned into a Lynx, While Attacking Triptolemus
artworks.description: Tempesta's companion plate (LACMA): King Lyncus tries to murder the sleeping Triptolemus and steal Demeter's gift; Ceres transforms the assassin into a lynx — Ovid's cautionary sequel to the chariot of grain.

popCulture.title: Triptolemus
popCulture.description: Demeter's Eleusinian envoy — the youth in the winged chariot who carries grain and the Mysteries' gift of agriculture.

popCulture.title: Homeric Hymn to Demeter
popCulture.description: The hymn names Triptolemus among Demeter's Eleusinian hosts — the mortal who receives the goddess's teaching.
